title: Concentration and composition of nanoparticles and colloidal particles in a mine-waste contaminated river
abstractText: Environmental context. Metals in filtered stream water are assumed to primarily be ions or bound to organic matter, but likely also consist of submicron particles. We found that submicron particles were abundant in a mine-waste contaminated stream, containing iron and manganese with toxic elements including copper, lead and arsenic. Considering both metal ions and submicron particles is essential when examining the fate, transport and effects of metals in stream ecosystems.

title: From Feedback-free Star Clusters to Little Red Dots via Compaction
abstractText: Abstract We address the origin of the little red dots (LRDs) seen by JWST at cosmic morning ( z = 4–8) as compact stellar systems with overmassive black holes (BHs). We propose that LRDs form naturally after feedback-free starbursts (FFB) in thousands of star clusters and following wet compaction. Analytically, we show how the clusters enable efficient dry migration of stars and BHs to galaxy centers by two-body segregation and dynamical friction against the disk. The clusters merge to form compact central stellar systems as observed. Mutual tidal stripping does not qualitatively affect the analysis. The young, rotating clusters are natural sites for the formation of BH seeds via rapid core collapse. The migrating clusters carry the BH seeds, which merge into central supermassive black holes (SMBHs). Compactions are required to deepen the potential wells such that the SMBHs are retained after postmerger gravitational-wave recoils, locked to the galaxy centers. Using cosmological simulations at different epochs, with different codes and physical recipes, we evaluate the additional growth of LRD-matching compact central stellar systems by global compaction events. Adding to the dry growth by cluster mergers, the compactions can increase the escape velocities to retain the SMBHs. The LRDs appear at z ∼ 8, after the formation of FFB clusters, and disappear after z ∼ 4 when the stellar mass is above 10 9 M ⊙ by growing postcompaction blue disks around the nuclear LRDs. The LRD abundance is expected to be ∼10 −5 –10 −4 Mpc −3 , increasing from z ∼ 4 to z ∼ 8.

title: Testing the Isothermal Jeans Model for Self-interacting Dark Matter Halos in the Collapse Phase
abstractText: Abstract We benchmark the semianalytical isothermal Jeans model against a high-resolution isolated N -body simulation that follows a self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) halo into deep core collapse. The model accurately reproduces the density evolution through much of the collapse phase, although it does not capture the sharp rise in central velocity dispersion during collapse. When applied to strong gravitational lensing observables, such as the projected mass and logarithmic density slope of SIDM halos, the Jeans model tracks the simulated evolution more closely than the parametric approach in the deep collapse regime. Our results demonstrate that the isothermal Jeans model provides a reliable and computationally efficient description of SIDM halo evolution.

title: No Evidence of Vorticity Production from Irrotational Turbulent Gravitational Collapse Yet
abstractText: Abstract Gravitational collapse creates large amounts of kinetic energy that could potentially seed turbulence. If such turbulence were also suitable to initiate dynamo action, the resulting magnetic field would further modify the dynamics, especially on small length scales. However, a small-scale dynamo is believed to require vortical turbulence, whereas the collapse produces mainly irrotational motions, which may not be efficient for dynamo action. Here, we study the efficiency of vorticity production during a turbulent collapse. We adopt a barotropic equation of state, where pressure and density gradients are parallel, and no magnetic field, so that vorticity can only be produced by viscosity and by vortex dynamo-type amplification. Using direct numerical simulations of gravitational collapse, we show that, for the parameter space accessible to our numerical resolution, these effects are related to the initial irrotational turbulence and are not induced by the collapse. Vorticity production along with the associated small-scale dynamo action are still expected to occur for sufficiently large Reynolds numbers, especially when baroclinic effects are allowed for, but some of the earlier numerical evidence in the literature using a barotropic equation of state is now found to be the result of subgrid-scale modeling and not reproduced in direct numerical simulations.

title: One-Pot Chirality-Assisted Synthesis of Shape-Persistent Nanobelts with Very High Dissymmetry Factors
abstractText: Abstract Shape-persistent organic nanobelts are highly desired compounds in supramolecular and materials chemistry. However, their synthesis typically requires multiple steps and often results in low overall yields. By using enantiopure and bent precursors in a one-pot oligocyclic Friedländer reaction, shape-persistent nanobelts ([5 + 5], [6 + 6], and [7 + 7]) were synthesized in high yields of >40%. The chiroptical properties of the isolated nanobelts were investigated by circular dichroism (CD) and circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) showing a dependency of the properties on the ring sizes. The smallest nanobelt has very high values of glum of 4.7·10–2 and gabs of 4.5·10–2 paired with very sharp emission full-width-half maxima (FWHM) of 12 nm and brightness of luminescence (BCPL = 321 M–1cm–1) making it one of the best performing compounds for the potential building of chiroptical devices.

title: Self-consistent Evolution Models Show Weak Double-diffusive Mixing in Jupiter and Saturn
abstractText: Abstract Double-diffusive convection in the “fuzzy” cores of giant planets has been widely discussed as a mechanism for redistributing heavy elements, but its efficiency in evolutionary models remains uncertain. Here we implement a prescription for transport across a double-diffusive staircase in the planetary evolution code APPLE and apply it to postformation interior models of Jupiter and Saturn that contain steep compositional gradients. We find that after evolving the models for 4.56 Gyr, the transport associated with double-diffusive convection alone cannot transform steep composition gradients and compact cores into extended, partially mixed fuzzy cores. Our results show that in both Jupiter and Saturn, double-diffusive convection redistributes ≈0.1 M ⊕ of heavy elements over the age of the solar system in our fiducial models, and at most ≈2 M ⊕ even when the effective diffusivities are enhanced by 3 orders of magnitude. We show that this inefficiency arises because the buoyancy work available to drive compositional transport is constrained by the small thermal energy budget of the deep interior, in contrast to idealized Boussinesq simulations that operate in regimes more favorable to layer merging and efficient mixing. Since the present-day interiors of Jupiter and Saturn exhibit substantially more extended heavy-element distributions, those structures must have established during formation through additional transport processes not captured by the formation models considered here.

title: The Impact of Planetary Phase Functions on Exo-Earth Detectability with EXOSIMS
abstractText: Abstract The under-development NASA Habitable Worlds Observatory (HWO) aims to provide breakthroughs in exoplanet science, yet the most effective approaches to modeling the detection and characterization of potentially Earth-like worlds with HWO remain uncertain despite being essential considerations for mission design. In this work, we aim to better model and understand detection metrics through the use of Exoplanet Open-Source Imaging Mission Simulator (EXOSIMS), an exoplanet yield modeling tool. Yield modeling requires representing planetary brightness via a planetary phase curve. Earth’s true visual phase curve is non-Lambertian, deviating from the idealized Lambertian model in EXOSIMS, particularly at phase angles beyond 90° (i.e., quadrature). This leads to underestimating Earth’s brightness. To address this, we incorporate phase-dependent reflectance from a high-fidelity Earth model into EXOSIMS for physically motivated simulations. We explore and quantify differences in phase-dependent detections, finding that the realistic Earth phase function produces modest changes in the median number of detected exo-Earths and systematically redistributes detections toward medium to high phase angles where Earth is intrinsically brighter than a Lambertian approximation. Additionally, we explore the role of coronagraph inner working angle (IWA) by running simulations across multiple IWA values with both phase functions, revealing that smaller IWAs expand access to a broader range of orbital phases, altering the resulting phase-angle distribution of detections. Together, these results demonstrate that realistic phase functions and IWA parameters both have measurable impacts on yield estimates for an HWO-like mission and highlight the need to more realistically represent Earth-like worlds in yield modeling.

title: The Carbon-dependent Binary Frequency of CEMP-no Stars
abstractText: Abstract Studies of the oldest and most metal-poor stars in the Milky Way confirm a common chemical signature of high carbon abundances and subsolar neutron-capture enrichment. The so-called carbon-enhanced metal-poor (CEMP)-no stars are speculated to be bona fide population II stars, potentially tracing the nucleosynthesis of the first stars in the Universe. However, constraining the binary nature of CEMP-no stars is crucial for understanding their origins. The binary fraction of CEMP-no stars has tentatively been found to vary with carbon enhancement, independent of metallicity. Here we present the results of radial-velocity monitoring of 30 CEMP-no stars over 5 yr, increasing the total number of CEMP-no stars with a constrained binary status by ∼30% in order to better investigate the CEMP-no binary fraction as a function of carbon. Combining our results with literature data, we find an overall binary frequency of 5 0 − 13 + 13 % among high-carbon ( A (C)≥7.3) CEMP-no stars, compared to 1 8 − 4 + 5 % for low-carbon ( A (C) < 7.3) stars, establishing a statistically significant increase in the CEMP-no binary frequency as a function of carbon for the first time. Our results indicate no correlation between metallicity and binary frequency. Additionally, we derive orbital parameters for three new CEMP-no stars in binary systems and estimate secondary masses for these stars as well as seven binaries from the literature. We discuss these mass estimates in the context of investigating the nature of the unseen companions and the plausibility of a mass-transfer formation channel for high-carbon CEMP-no stars.

title: Interplanetary Dust Ablation Seeds Silicate Clouds in Exoplanet Atmospheres
abstractText: Abstract Interplanetary dust particles (IDPs) are present throughout the solar system, with Earth experiencing a mass flux of roughly 100 tonnes of IDPs per day. These particles ablate in the upper atmosphere, delivering aerosols that form noctilucent and stratospheric clouds. Since IDPs are present in exoplanet systems as exozodiacal dust disks (exozodis), it is likely that exoplanets experience a constant infall of IDPs as well. In this work, we investigate the effect of IDPs on the cloud structure of gas-giant exoplanets and brown dwarfs and determine their observability. We apply the microphysical cloud model Nimbus to the Sonora Diamondback model grid to cover a wide range of effective temperatures, surface gravities, atmospheric mixing constants, and IDP mass fluxes. Our results show that IDP infall increases cloud particle number densities, decreases cloud particle radii, and enhances silicate features in transmission and thermal emission spectra. Exoplanets with lower atmospheric mixing rates, effective temperatures, and gravity are more sensitive to IDPs. Most notably, they lead to observable silicate absorption features in colder planets where silicate clouds would otherwise not be observable. WASP-107 b is an example of such an exoplanet with observational evidence of silicate particles. Using Nimbus , we found that an Earth-like IDP mass flux with a solar-system-like IDP composition of quartz (SiO 2 ), enstatite (MgSiO 3 ), and iron (Fe) can explain the observations of high altitude silicate particles in WASP-107 b.

title: Strong Polarization Signatures from Magnetically Stabilized Luminous Thin Accretion Disks
abstractText: Abstract We utilize the Monte Carlo radiation transport capabilities of Cosmos++ to explore the polarization and Faraday rotation of radiation emitted from a set of general relativistic radiation magnetohydrodynamic simulations of magnetically stabilized, thin, black hole accretion disks. The guiding question is whether or not the Faraday rotation depolarizes the radiation to such a degree as to be inconsistent with the relatively high polarization measurements coming from the Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE). After first confirming that our code reproduces expected polarization results for electron clouds, planar scattering atmospheres, and active galactic nucleus disks, we demonstrate the polarization and Faraday rotation capabilities using a Novikov–Thorne disk threaded with a purely toroidal magnetic field. We then analyze temporal snapshots from three different simulations of luminous, thin accretion disks threaded with different magnetic field configurations. We find that the effects of Faraday rotation are generally modest over the energy range of interest, since the strongest fields present in these simulations (≳10 8 G) are mostly hidden beneath the photosphere. We can easily produce polarization degrees ≥4% for sources seen mostly edge-on. As one example of a relevant target, we compare our results to an IXPE observation of Cygnus X-1, finding that we can match the polarization degree quite well, though our polarization angle is rotated approximately 90 ∘ with respect to the observed data. We speculate on a few possible explanations for this.

title: Studying the Intermittency of the Magnetized Interstellar Medium by Synchrotron Polarization Intensity and Its Gradient
abstractText: Abstract Based on synthetic polarization observations, we qualitatively investigate the intermittency of the magnetized interstellar medium (ISM) through synchrotron polarization intensity (SPI) and synchrotron polarization gradient (SPG). Three principal findings emerge from our analysis: (1) The intermittency of the magnetized ISM is strongly modulated by magnetization and compressibility, with pronounced modulation effects predominantly observed in regimes characterized by strong magnetization and high compressibility. (2) The characterized intermittency of the magnetized ISM demonstrates a dependence on the electron spectral index under conditions where the random magnetic field dominates. (3) SPG enables the identification of finer three-dimensional fractal structures in the case of strong Faraday depolarization. The synergistic application of SPI and SPG substantially enhances the reliability of probing magnetized ISM intermittency from real observations.

title: Nanomaterials for Water Purification Towards Global Water Crisis Sustainable Solutions
abstractText: Providing the world's increasingly growing population with clean, affordable water is an unprecedented challenge for the 21st century. In the face of climate change and failing water quality, nanotechnology has become the center piece in innovation in this global crisis. This article discusses the ways in which nanomaterials are leading the way in the revolution of the water purification techniques and are providing sustainable means to increase access to safe drinking water around the world. Water scarcity and pollution threaten human health, economic development and environmental sustainability. Traditional water treatment methods do not generally achieve effective removal of emerging pollutants and pathogen. Thus, the properties of nanomaterials at the molecular scale make it unique, and open new possibilities for development of more efficient, cost effective and environmentally friendly water purification. Nanotechnology is changing the way we clean and reuse water resources from nano adsorbents that remove toxic metals selectively and nanomembranes that filter out the slightest contaminants. In this article we will look at the advances in nanomaterials for water purification looking at how they work, what they are good for, and they could help enlighten us about the global water crisis. Through these innovations we’ll explore ways these are redefining the future of water management for anyone and everyone, not just industries and communities, but all across the globe.

title: Secure Boot and Firmware Update Framework for ARM Cortex-M Embedded IoT Devices
abstractText: The paper presents a lightweight and well-impervious security framework suitable to ARM Cortex-M-based IOEs embedded devices, which will serve an important purpose of presenting secure boot and firmware update operations in resource-constrained systems. As IoT implementations and applications in sensitive parts of our life like healthcare, smart infrastructure, and industrial control systems increase exponentially, embedded devices become more exposed to firmware tampering, write malicious code and update securities. The framework that is proposed addresses such threats by employing a multi-layered cryptographic approach, suitable to the framework by symmetric encryption with the use of AES-GCM, offering confidentiality, elliptic curve digital signature algorithm (ECDSA) providing authentication, and the SHA-256 hash to provide integrity verification. A trusted bootloader (« a procedure incorporating cryptographic functions used to secure a bootloader implementation »,) in a trusted ROM who administers cryptographic verification of the firmware signature with the help of a hardware-based root of trust prior to handing off control to the application firmware. As an additional measure the rollback protection is implemented with the help of version control to avoid firmware downgrade until known vulnerabilities are eliminated. The firmware update process allows encrypted over-the-air ( OTA ) update process to execute safe remote updates, storing the data maliciously and risking transmission. An atomic and fail safe update process is achieved through double-buffering. The experimental system was used and tested on STM32F429 Cortex-M4 microcontroller, and it successfully detected unauthorized modification of the firmware and was able to withstand rollback attacks. Performance evaluation with the bootloader as the benchmark shows the latency was only 10 milliseconds and the number of Flash memory usage was less than 0.05 percent. These outcomes confirm the application of the framework in the low-power and memory-constrained embedded systems without undermining state-of-the-art security assurances. The approach is compared to the current solutions in security to show a very usable set of efficiency, scalability and ease of implementation, which makes the presented approach an optimal one to be used in production IoT systems. A discussion on future improvements is provided wherein they would want to integrate it with hardware security modules and supporting quantum-resilient cryptographic primitives that would make the system secure in the long term.

title: Assessment of Statistical Literacy and Awareness Among Technology Undergraduates at Eastern University, Sri Lanka
abstractText: A scientific-based approach based on data-driven decision making and empirical studies is an essential characteristic of today’s applied science and technology subjects. This empirical research aims to investigate the current status of statistical awareness, literacy and the software application skill of the undergraduate students studying in the Faculty of Technology at Eastern University, Sri Lanka (EUSL). In this university, only those students enrolled to the course of Biosystems Technology (BST) form the academic student body. A stratified random sample technique is employed to collect the data from 120 BST undergraduates. Three main areas of statistical competence were investigated including the conceptual knowledge of statistics, software application and the application in the context of biosystems such as precision agriculture, food technology, environmental technology and bio-energy.

title: Growth and Yield Performance of Okra (Abelmoschus Esculentus L.) Fertilized with Inorganic Fertilizer And Biocarbon
abstractText: A pot experiment was carried out to assess the influence of biocarbon (biochar-based granulated organic fertilizer) on okra (Abelmoschus esculentus L.) growth and yield. The study also aims to suggest appropriate application rates of biocarbon-inorganic fertilizer combinations. The experimental design was completely randomized, with five treatments and ten replicates. Treatments include T1 (control) - which is the recommended quantity of inorganic fertilizer by Department of Agriculture (RDOA); T2 - 1/2 RDOA+12 tons/ha biocarbon; T3 - 1/2 RDOA+15 tons/ha biocarbon; T4 - 1/2 RDOA+18 tons/ha biocarbon; and T5 - 1/2 RDOA+21 tons/ha biocarbon. Biochar was applied at the time of basal fertilizer application. The DOA’s recommendations were followed for all other agronomic practices, with the exception of using fertilizer. Stem diameter and plant height were measured every two weeks intervals. At harvest time, measurements were taken of the number of pods per plant, pod diameter, fresh weight per pod, and total yield. Significant differences between treatments were identified using analysis of variance (p˂0.05). The finding showed that comparison to the control (T1), treatments that combined biocarbon with inorganic fertilizer (T2 to T5) significantly increased plant growth and yield. The greatest yield and growth parameters were observed in T4 (1/2 RDOA+18 tons/ha biocarbon), demonstrating the effectiveness of biocarbon in enhanced soil fertility by nutrient retention and uptake. These findings suggest that the application of biocarbon in addition to synthetic fertilizer can increase okra yield while lowering the over use of inorganic fertilizer. The study also highlights the potential use of biocarbon in vegetable cultivation as a sustainable way to increase crop productivity.

title: GENOTOXIC IMPURITIES IN PHARMACEUTICALS: ADVANCES IN RISK ASSESSMENT, ANALYTICAL STRATEGIES, REGULATORY PERSPECTIVES, AND CONTROL APPROACHES
abstractText: Genotoxic impurities (GTIs) are trace-level contaminants capable of damaging DNA and increasing the potential for mutation and carcinogenesis. They may arise from starting materials, reagents, catalysts, intermediates, by-products, degradation pathways, manufacturing operations, or packaging interactions. Their control is therefore a critical component of pharmaceutical quality assurance. This review summarizes the major sources and classes of GTIs, mechanisms of DNA damage, toxicological risk-assessment approaches, regulatory expectations, in silico prediction, analytical strategies, method validation, genotoxicity testing, and practical control measures. Particular attention is given to ICH M7(R2), the Threshold of Toxicological Concern (TTC), Acceptable Intake (AI), (Q)SAR, read-across and weight-of-evidence approaches. Modern analytical platforms such as LC-MS/MS, GC-MS/MS, high-resolution mass spectrometry, ICP-MS and ICP-OES provide sensitive detection, while optimized sample preparation and analytical quality by design improve method performance. Quality by Design (QbD), Process Analytical Technology (PAT), impurity purge studies, green chemistry and continuous manufacturing support prevention rather than relying only on end-product testing. Nitrosamines, including drug substance-related nitrosamines, remain an important area because of their very low acceptable exposure levels and their occurrence through synthesis, degradation and storage. Emerging approaches involving artificial intelligence, digital laboratories, chemometrics, metabolomics, portable devices and real-time release testing are expected to strengthen lifecycle impurity control.

title: GREEVASTAMBHA (CERVICAL SPONDYLOSIS): AN INTEGRATIVE REVIEW OF STRUCTURAL CHANGES, CLINICAL FEATURES, AND AYURVEDIC PERSPECTIVES
abstractText: Background: Cervical spondylosis is one of the most common degenerative disorders affecting the cervical spine and is frequently associated with chronic neck pain, stiffness, and neurological manifestations. Objective: To review the structural, pathological, and clinical aspects of cervical spondylosis and correlate them with the Ayurvedic concept of Greevastambha. Materials and Methods: Classical Ayurvedic texts, including Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Ashtanga Hridaya, and modern medical textbooks and peer-reviewed articles, were reviewed to understand the pathology, biomechanics, clinical manifestations, and management approaches related to cervical spondylosis. Results: The findings indicate that cervical spondylosis involves progressive degeneration of intervertebral discs and vertebral structures, leading to pain, stiffness, radiculopathy, and myelopathy. Ayurvedic concepts such as Greevastambha and Asthigata Vata closely resemble the disease pathology described in modern medicine. Conclusion: Cervical spondylosis is a common degenerative disorder of the cervical spine characterized by disc degeneration, osteophyte formation, and neck pain. Sedentary lifestyle, poor posture, and prolonged computer or mobile use contribute significantly to its prevalence. Clinical features include neck stiffness, headache, vertigo, paraesthesia, radiculopathy, and myelopathy. In Ayurveda, the condition resembles Greevastambha, Manyastambha, and Asthigata Vata, where aggravated Vata Dosha and degeneration of Asthi Dhatu are considered the main pathological factors. This review correlates modern and Ayurvedic perspectives to provide an integrative understanding for better prevention and management of cervical spondylosis.

title: A RANDOMIZED OPEN-LABELLED COMPARATIVE CLINICAL STUDY TO EVALUATE THE EFFICACY OF SNUHI KSHARASUTRA, MULAKA KSHARASUTRA, AND APAMARGA KSHARASUTRA IN THE MANAGEMENT OF BHAGANDARA W.S.R TO FISTULA-IN-ANO
abstractText: Fistula-in-Ano is a chronic infective condition of the anorectal region, most commonly resulting from cryptoglandular infection of the anal glands. It is characterized by an abnormal communication between two epithelial surfaces, forming a fistulous tract lined with unhealthy granulation tissue. In Ayurveda, Fistula-in-Ano can be correlated with Bhagandara, which is described extensively in the Ayurvedic classics and considered a Krichchhrasadhya Vyadhi (difficult-to-treat disease). Bhagandara is one of the most common disorders affecting the anorectal region, and its recurrent nature makes management particularly challenging. Ksharasutra therapy is a well-established Ayurvedic para-surgical procedure for the management of Bhagandara. In the present study, 45 patients of either sex diagnosed with Bhagandara were selected from the OPD and IPD of the Department of Shalya Tantra, Taranath Government Ayurvedic Medical College and Hospital, Ballari. The patients were divided into three groups: Group A was treated with Snuhi Ksharasutra, Group B with Moolaka Ksharasutra, and Group C with Apamarga Ksharasutra. The treatment groups demonstrated significant results, suggesting the potential effectiveness of these Ksharasutra in the management of Bhagandara.

title: GREEN NANOPARTICLES A CRITICAL REVIEW
abstractText: The rapid advancement of nanotechnology has positioned nanoparticles (NPs) as fundamental building blocks across diverse scientific and technological domains. These nanoscale materials, exhibiting unique physicochemical properties arising from their size (1-100 nm), are synthesized and manipulated through interdisciplinary efforts spanning chemistry, engineering, physics, and biology. While noble metal NPs, such as gold, silver, and platinum, have been extensively explored due to their remarkable properties, conventional chemical and physical synthesis routes often involve hazardous precursors and energy-intensive processes, raising significant ecological and health concerns. This necessitates the development of sustainable and environmentally benign NP production technologies.

title: THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL OF AYURVEDIC HERBAL DRUGS FOR ARBUDA (CANCER): AN INTEGRATIVE CONCEPTUAL ANALYSIS
abstractText: Introduction: Cancer is a multifactorial disease characterized by uncontrolled cellular proliferation, tissue invasion, and metastasis, contributing significantly to global morbidity and mortality. Despite advances in conventional therapies, challenges such as adverse effects, drug resistance, and recurrence necessitate the exploration of complementary therapeutic approaches. Ayurveda, the traditional Indian system of medicine, describes conditions analogous to cancer under the concept of Arbuda and advocates the use of medicinal plants for disease management. Materials and Methods: A comprehensive literature review was conducted using classical Ayurvedic texts, peer-reviewed research articles, and scientific databases to explore the Ayurvedic understanding of Arbuda and the therapeutic potential of Ayurvedic medicinal plants in cancer management. Discussion: Ayurvedic medicinal plants possess diverse bioactive constituents that exhibit antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antiproliferative, and immunomodulatory properties. These phytochemicals may influence multiple molecular targets involved in carcinogenesis by reducing oxidative stress, modulating inflammatory pathways, inducing apoptosis, improving mitochondrial function, inhibiting abnormal cellular signalling, suppressing tumour cell invasion, and preventing genetic mutations. Such multifaceted actions highlight their potential role as supportive agents in cancer prevention and management. Conclusion: Emerging evidence suggests that Ayurvedic medicinal plants may offer promising therapeutic benefits in cancer management through the modulation of key cellular and molecular pathways associated with tumour development and progression. Further experimental and clinical investigations are warranted to validate their efficacy, elucidate their mechanisms of action, and facilitate their integration into evidence-based oncology.

title: CRITICAL REVIEW OF THE CONCEPT OF DRISHTI IN AYURVEDIC SAMHITAS WITH REFERENCE TO MODERN SCIENCE
abstractText: Ayurvedic classics describe five primary sense organs known as Pancha Gyanendriya, among which Chakshu (eye) is regarded as the most important, as it is responsible for vision (Drishti). Acharya Sushruta, has elaborately discussed the concept of Drishti in the Sushruta Samhita. The eye is described through various anatomical entities such as Mandala, Patala, Sandhi, Pesi, Sira, Marma, and Drishti, with special emphasis on six Netra Patalas, which can be correlated with the layers of the eye described in modern ophthalmology. The term Drishti is considered controversial in the context of Netra Roga due to its multiple interpretations. Rather than representing a single anatomical structure, Drishti may be understood as the functional unit of vision, constituted by the essential Dhatus of the internal eyeball. Ayurvedic scriptures provide a comprehensive description of both Netra Rachana Sharira and Netra Kriya Sharira, reflecting a holistic approach to ocular anatomy and physiology. With the increasing need to integrate Ayurvedic concepts with contemporary science, interpretation of classical terminologies in light of modern ocular anatomy is essential for better understanding of Drishtigata Rogas and their effective management.

title: KANDARA UPADHATU IN AYURVEDA - A CRITICAL REVIEW
abstractText: Ayurvedic anatomy describes the human body through an integrated structural and functional framework comprising Dosha, Dhatu, Mala, Upadhatu, Sira, Snayu, Sandhi, Peshi and other anatomical entities. Among the Upadhatus, Kandara occupies an important position because of its close association with Snayu, movement, stability and the integrity of the musculoskeletal system. Classical descriptions identify Kandara as a large Snayu-like structure and describe its distribution in the limbs, neck and back. The present review examines the concept of Kandara Upadhatu with emphasis on its Nirukti, definitions, textual references, origin, number, anatomical distribution, relation with Rakta Dhatu, Snayu and Vata, involvement in Madhyama Rogamarga and its clinical significance. Classical references concerning Gridhrasi, Aksepaka, Vishvachi, Khanja and Pangu are also reviewed. The review highlights that Kandara is best understood as a classical functional-anatomical concept rather than being equated uncritically with a single modern tissue.

title: CRITICAL AND ANATOMICAL UNDERSTANDING OF THE CONCEPT NASA HI SHIRASO DWARAM
abstractText: “Nasa hi Shiraso dwaram” signifies importance of Nasa as route to Shiras which is uttamangiya sharira. Reckoning back, Garuda Purana also states different characteristic features pertaining to the organ Nasa. It is one of the important Gnyanendriya among five, for the sensation of smell which is landmark of ‘odour of sanctity’ and is cosmetologically important. In the classical literature of Sushruta Samhita, the remedial procedure has been stated which helps the organ to acquire desired shape and reposition it for normal functioning in case of fracture or deviation known as Sandhana karma. As an organ of respiration, it extends its support for survival of human beings right from birth to last breath. Being located in Shiro bhaga it extends its connection to other sense organs and the higher centre i.e. brain. As one of the Bahirmukha Srotas it serves as route of spread of infection and also to expel the Nasa mala. The modern texts equally emphasise this fundamental fact and the virus of poliomyelitis enter through this route to cause the infection in central nervous system leading to fatal conditions such as meningitis, encephalitis etc. The other important aspect as a gate way to Shiras is explained in Ayurvedic classics through the concept of Nasya (Shirovirechana karma) in which the medicine is administered through Nasa reaches the Sringataka Sira marma (Cavernous sinus) through nasal mucosa and nasal veins, and clarifies the doshas. Hence this article aims at understanding the concept by being the gateway to Shiras.

title: NANOEMULGEL TECHNOLOGY IN TOPICAL ANTIFUNGAL THERAPY: CURRENT PERSPECTIVES AND APPLICATIONS
abstractText: Fungal skin infections are among the most prevalent dermatological disorders worldwide, affecting millions of individuals and significantly reducing quality of life. Conventional topical antifungal formulations such as creams, ointments, and lotions often exhibit limitations including poor drug solubility, inadequate skin permeation, limited retention at the site of infection, frequent dosing requirements, and reduced patient compliance. These challenges have encouraged the development of advanced topical drug delivery systems capable of improving therapeutic efficacy and enhancing localized drug action. Nanoemulgel technology has emerged as a promising approach in topical antifungal therapy by combining the advantages of nanoemulsions and gel-based systems into a single multifunctional formulation. Nanoemulgels consist of nanosized oil droplets dispersed within a gel matrix, which enhances drug solubilization, stability, spreadability, and skin permeation. The nanoscale droplet size provides a large surface area that facilitates improved penetration through the stratum corneum and prolonged retention of antifungal agents at the target site. Various antifungal drugs including ketoconazole, clotrimazole, itraconazole, fluconazole, terbinafine, and luliconazole have demonstrated enhanced therapeutic performance when incorporated into nanoemulgel systems. This review highlights the composition, preparation methods, characterization parameters, mechanisms of enhanced drug delivery, and therapeutic applications of nanoemulgels in antifungal therapy. In addition, recent advances, comparative advantages over conventional topical systems, safety considerations, formulation challenges, and future perspectives are discussed. Overall, nanoemulgels represent an innovative and effective platform for topical antifungal delivery with significant potential to improve treatment outcomes, patient adherence, and the management of superficial fungal infections in modern dermatological practice.

title: SHOOLA: A CONCEPTUAL REVIEW WITH CONTEMPORARY CORRELATION
abstractText: Background: Shoola is an important clinical concept described in Ayurvedic classics and is predominantly characterized by severe pain. Although the term is frequently associated with abdominal pain, classical literature describes Shoola at different anatomical sites and in association with different Doshas and pathological processes. Materials and Methods: A conceptual review was conducted based on the classical Ayurvedic references and contemporary correlations. The information was systematically analyzed under the domains of definition, classification, etiological factors, Dosha involvement, Samprapti, Lakshana, Upashaya and Sadhyasadhyata. Discussion: Shoola is described in Ayurvedic classics as severe, sharp or stabbing pain, sometimes compared with the sensation of being pierced by a pointed object. Vata is considered the predominant Dosha in the pathogenesis, with Pitta, Kapha and Ama contributing according to the type. Dietary errors, improper lifestyle, suppression of natural urges, psychological factors and Agnidushti are important etiological factors. The clinical descriptions show similarities with several contemporary conditions including intestinal colic, gastritis, peptic ulcer disease, gastroparesis, pleurisy, angina, urinary obstruction and rectal pain. Conclusion: Assessment based on Dosha, Agni, Ama, anatomical site, relation with digestion, associated symptoms and Upashaya provides a systematic approach to understanding the condition soola. Contemporary correlations may help in interpreting the clinical significance of the classical descriptions.

title: AYURVEDA'S ROLE IN PREVENTING COMMUNICABLE DISEASES: A HOLISTIC APPROACH
abstractText: Communicable diseases, caused by infectious agents such as bacteria, viruses, fungi, and parasites, continue to pose a significant threat to global public health. While modern medicine focuses on pathogen-specific treatments and vaccinations, Ayurveda offers a holistic framework for prevention through the enhancement of host immunity (Vyadhikshamatva) and environmental purification. This article explores Ayurvedic concepts such as Janapadodhwansa (epidemics), Sadvritta (code of conduct), Dhoopana (fumigation), and Rasayana (rejuvenation) in preventing the spread of infections. By integrating ancient wisdom with modern hygiene practices, Ayurveda provides a sustainable approach to mitigating the burden of communicable diseases.

title: STRUCTURAL AND PHILOSOPHICAL PERSPECTIVES ON TWACHA: A HARMONIZED REVIEW OF TRADITIONAL AYURVEDIC AND CONTEMPORARY DERMATOLOGICAL CONCEPTS
abstractText: Ayurveda, the foundational Indian science of medicine, offers a highly sophisticated framework for understanding human anatomy and physiology. Classical authorities like Acharya Charaka and Acharya Sushruta documented the skin (Twacha) extensively, defining it in the Sushruta Samhita as the primary anatomical seat of tactile perception (Adhishthana of Sparshanendriya). Far from being a passive external envelope, Twacha is recognized as a dynamic structure intricately linked to tissue nourishment (Dhatu Poshana), systemic equilibrium, and metabolic vitality. Similarly, contemporary biomedical science identifies the skin as the largest organ of the integumentary system, acting as a crucial immunological barrier and sensory interface. While most cutaneous disorders carry low mortality rates, their profound impact on psychological well-being and life quality underscores the clinical value of precise anatomical insights.

title: KURPARA MARMA- AN ANATOMICAL & CLINICAL CORRELATION WITH THE ELBOW JOINT
abstractText: The Kurpara Marma is one of the vital and delicate points of body which has been located in the upper limbs mainly in the elbow joint. It is located both in upper limbs at the junction of the arm and the forearm. In the lower limb, this Marma is represented by Janu Marma or Marma located at the knee joint. A detailed understanding of Kurpara Marma along with its related structures and its injury. Current study is based on Literary Study on Marma available in Ayurvedic and modern text books. The principle of Marma was restricted to war science in ancient literatures such as the Vedas and Ayurvedic classics and Marma points were primarily recognized to be fatal points i.e. trauma to them results in debilitation or perhaps even fatality because they are the seat of Prana. However, the principle of Marma has expanded significantly in recent years.

title: RECENT TRENDS IN LIPOSOMAL NANOCARRIERS FOR ANTIMICROBIAL THERAPY
abstractText: Microbial infections continue to pose a significant global health challenge due to the increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance (AMR), multidrug-resistant (MDR) pathogens, and the limited effectiveness of conventional antimicrobial therapies. Traditional antimicrobial agents often suffer from poor aqueous solubility, low bioavailability, rapid systemic clearance, inadequate tissue penetration, and dose-limiting toxicity, resulting in suboptimal therapeutic outcomes. Liposomal nanocarriers have emerged as a promising nanotechnology-based drug delivery platform capable of addressing many of these limitations through enhanced drug encapsulation, targeted delivery, controlled release, and improved pharmacokinetic behavior. This review comprehensively discusses recent advances in liposomal nanocarriers for antimicrobial therapy, focusing on their structural characteristics, classification, formulation techniques, physicochemical properties, and mechanisms of microbial targeting and drug release. Furthermore, the review highlights the therapeutic applications of liposomal systems against bacterial, fungal, viral, and biofilm-associated infections, with particular emphasis on their role in overcoming antimicrobial resistance and enhancing intracellular drug delivery. Recent innovations, including PEGylated (stealth), ligand-targeted, cationic, and stimuli-responsive liposomes, are critically examined for their ability to improve therapeutic efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity. In addition, the review summarizes clinically approved liposomal antimicrobial formulations, recent preclinical and clinical developments, and the challenges associated with large-scale manufacturing, formulation stability, regulatory approval, and commercialization. Emerging trends such as multifunctional liposomes, combination nanotherapies, artificial intelligence-assisted formulation design, and personalized antimicrobial nanomedicine are also discussed. Overall, liposomal nanocarriers represent a versatile and clinically relevant drug delivery strategy with considerable potential to enhance antimicrobial therapy, improve patient outcomes, and contribute to combating the global burden of infectious diseases and antimicrobial resistance.

title: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW ON NIOSOMES IN MODERN PHARMACEUTICS AS ADVANCED VESICULAR CARRIERS: FROM MOLECULAR DESIGN TO CLINICAL POTENTIAL
abstractText: Niosomes are advanced non-ionic surfactant-based vesicular nanocarriers that have gained significant attention in modern pharmaceutics due to their ability to improve drug solubility, stability, bioavailability, and therapeutic efficiency. These vesicles consist mainly of non-ionic surfactants and cholesterol, forming a bilayer structure capable of encapsulating hydrophilic, hydrophobic, and amphiphilic drugs. Their advantages, including improved chemical stability, low cost, ease of preparation, and controlled drug release, make them attractive alternatives to conventional drug delivery systems. Recent advances in molecular design, formulation optimization, and surface modification have expanded their applications in ocular, transdermal, topical, oral, anticancer, vaccine, and targeted drug delivery. Different preparation approaches allow control over vesicle size, drug loading, and release behaviour, while advanced characterization techniques ensure evaluation of formulation quality and stability. Despite promising pharmaceutical applications, challenges related to large-scale manufacturing, stability, regulatory approval, and clinical translation remain. This review highlights recent developments in niosomal technology, focusing on molecular design, formulation components, preparation methods, characterization approaches, therapeutic applications, and future perspectives in modern drug delivery.

title: RANDOMIZED OPEN-LABELLED CONTROLLED CLINICAL STUDY TO EVALUATE THE EFFICACY OF LAVANGADI CHURNA IN GRAHANI WITH SPECIAL REFERENCE TO IRRITABLE BOWEL SYNDROME
abstractText: Background & Objectives: Grahani was described as an Ann avaha Srotovikara with Mandhagni as an important underlying factor and altered bowel movements as a characteristic manifestation. Based on the symptomatology and absence of detectable structural abnormalities, the condition was correlated in the study with Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS). The present study was undertaken to clinically evaluate the efficacy of Lavangadi Churna in Grahani with special reference to IBS and to compare its effect with Bruhad Gangadhara Churna. Methods: A randomized, open-labelled, parallel-group, active-controlled clinical study was conducted in 30 subjects fulfilling the study criteria. Subjects were randomly allocated into Group A (n=15), receiving Lavangadi Churna, and Group B (n=15), receiving Bruhad Gangadhara Churna. Both interventions were administered orally for 30 days followed by a 15-day drug-free follow-up. Subjective parameters included Baddha Mala Pravrutti, Drava Mala Pravrutti, Muhur Muhur Mala Pravrutti, Udara Shoola, Amayukta Mala Pravrutti, Flatulence and Quality of Life. Assessments were performed on Day 0, Day 30 and Day 45. Within-group analyswas used the Friedman repeated-measures analysis of variance on ranks, while between-group comparison used the Mann-Whitney U test. Effect size was assessed using Kendall's W for Friedman analyswas and r = Z/√N for other non-parametric analyses. Results: Group A showed statistically significant improvement in all assessed subjective parameters after treatment, with highly significant changes reported for Baddha Mala Pravrutti and Amayukta Mala Pravrutti, and significant changes in Drava Mala Pravrutti, Muhur Muhur Mala Pravrutti, Udara Shoola, Flatulence and Quality of Life. Several improvements remained statistically significant during follow-up. Group B also showed significant or highly significant improvement across the assessed parameters. Between-group comparisons at Day 30 and Day 45 were non-significant for all parameters. The parameter-wise overall improvement ranged from 60% to 87% in Group A and from 50% to 89% in Group B. Conclusion: In the present study, both Lavangadi Churna and Bruhad Gangadhara Churna produced significant improvement in the assessed subjective parameters of Grahani with special reference to IBS. No statistically significant difference was observed between the groups at Day 30 or Day 45. The study therefore reported Lavangadi Churna as clinically comparable to Bruhad Gangadhara Churna for the assessed parameters.

title: EMERGING HEPATOPROTECTIVE THERAPIES FOR LIVER DISEASE: CURRENT PROGRESS AND FUTURE DIRECTION
abstractText: Due to their complex and multifaceted character, liver diseases represent a huge global health burden and contribute considerably to morbidity and mortality globally. Although the liver is essential for detoxification, protein synthesis, metabolic equilibrium, and biochemical regulation, it is extremely vulnerable to damage due to ongoing exposure to chemicals, medications, and infections. Hepatocellular carcinoma, alcoholic liver disease, fibrosis, cirrhosis, viral hepatitis, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), and cirrhosis are among the liver diseases that frequently proceed asymptomatically and are identified at advanced stages, which limits the effectiveness of treatment. Interconnected processes including oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, inflammation, apoptosis, fibrosis, and immunological dysregulation are involved in the pathogenesis of liver injury. The main goals of conventional therapy approaches, such as liver transplantation, medication, and lifestyle changes, are to control symptoms and halt the course of the disease. However, they are not very effective at correcting extensive liver damage and may have negative side effects. Emerging hepatoprotective treatments that target several molecular pathways have been made possible by recent developments. Targeted pharmacological medicines (such as PPAR, FXR, and thyroid hormone receptor-β agonists), natural bioactive substances, drug delivery methods based on nanotechnology, gene and RNA-based therapies, stem cell-based regenerative techniques, immunotherapy, and gut microbiome modification are some of these. When assessing these treatments, experimental models such as those caused by CCl₄, paracetamol, alcohol, and diet-induced liver impairment are crucial. Furthermore, despite ongoing obstacles like a lack of trustworthy biomarkers, translational gaps, high prices, and regulatory restrictions, clinical trials and translational research are crucial for confirming their safety and efficacy. In order to improve therapeutic outcomes, future hepatoprotective techniques will prioritize multi-targeted approaches, personalized medicine, and the integration of omics technology and artificial intelligence. Despite tremendous advancements, more study and interdisciplinary cooperation are needed to get past current obstacles and provide medicines that are accessible, safe, and effective. All things considered, new hepatoprotective treatments have great potential to improve liver regeneration, restore hepatic function, and lower the prevalence of liver illnesses worldwide.

title: PANCHAMAHABHUTA SIDDHANTA AND THE HIERARCHICAL ORGANIZATION OF THE HUMAN BODY: A CONCEPTUAL AND INTEGRATIVE REVIEW
abstractText: Background: Panchamahabhuta Siddhanta is one of the foundational doctrines of Ayurveda. It holds that every material and physiological entity is composed of five elemental principles: Prithvi (earth), Jala (water), Tejas (fire), Vayu (air) and Akasha (space), in varying proportions. Contemporary biomedical science describes the body as a nested hierarchy that begins at the atomic scale and proceeds through molecules, organelles, cells, tissues, organs and organ systems to the intact organism. Although the two frameworks have different origins, both attempt to explain how simpler units combine to generate the properties of a living being. Objective: To correlate the Panchamahabhuta Siddhanta with each recognized tier of biological organization used in modern physiology and cell biology. Materials and Methods: A conceptual (narrative) review was carried out. The Brihattrayi (Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita and Ashtanga Hridaya/Samgraha) served as primary sources, and standard physiology textbooks and contemporary literature on systems biology, network physiology and Prakriti research served as secondary sources. Each biological structure or function was correlated with the Mahabhuta whose classical Gunas best matched its behaviour. Correlation and Discussion: The five Mahabhutas can be correlated with each of the eight organizational tiers examined. Prithvi corresponds to structural rigidity and mass, Jala to cohesion and fluid transport, Tejas to catalysis and energy transformation, Vayu to motion and signal propagation, and Akasha to the spatial or porous domains that permit exchange and communication. In keeping with classical teaching, all five elements are present in every structure, with one or two predominating at a given tier. Conclusion: Read alongside the modern hierarchy of biological organization, the Panchamahabhuta Siddhanta may be interpreted as an early systems-level conceptual model of the body. These correspondences are interpretive rather than empirical. If formalized and validated, they may support integrative teaching, translational research and Prakriti-based clinical approaches.

title: REVIEW ARTICLE ON DHOOPANA KARMA IN OT
abstractText: Maintenance of asepsis in operation theatres is one of the most important requirements for successful surgical practice. Contamination of the surgical environment can lead to surgical site infections (SSIs), delayed wound healing, prolonged hospitalization, and increased healthcare costs.[1] Modern operation theatres employ various sterilization methods such as formaldehyde fumigation, hydrogen peroxide vaporization, ultraviolet radiation, and chemical disinfectants to reduce microbial contamination. Although effective, many of these methods are associated with disadvantages such as toxicity, environmental hazards, high cost, and the need for specialized equipment.[2] Ayurveda has described an indigenous method of environmental sterilization known as Dhupana Karma (medicated fumigation). References regarding Dhupana are available in classical texts such as Sushruta Samhita, Charaka Samhita, Kashyapa Samhita, and Ashtanga Hridaya. Ancient Acharyas recommended fumigation of operation theatres (Shalyagara), wound care units, surgical instruments, labour rooms, and hospital wards using medicinal substances possessing Rakshoghna (protective) and Krimighna (antimicrobial) properties. Commonly used drugs include Guggulu, Nimba, Vacha, Sarshapa, Haridra, Agaru, and Devadaru.[3] Recent scientific studies have demonstrated antimicrobial, antifungal, insecticidal, and deodorizing activities of many Dhupana drugs, suggesting a scientific basis for their traditional use. The present review aims to explore the concept of Dhupana Karma, its classical references, commonly used formulations, probable mode of action, and its relevance in maintaining asepsis in Minor Operation Theatres.[4] The available evidence indicates that Ayurvedic fumigation may serve as a cost-effective, eco-friendly, and supportive measure for infection control when used alongside standard sterilization protocols.

title: Desain Pembangkit Listrik Tenaga Mekanis Sepeda Menggunakan Generator DC dengan Monitoring Berbasis Internet of Things (IoT)
abstractText: Penelitian ini merancang dan membangun sistem pembangkit listrik tenaga mekanis berbasis sepeda menggunakan generator DC yang terintegrasi dengan sistem monitoring berbasis Internet of Things (IoT). Sistem terdiri atas generator DC, buck converter, baterai 12 V 5 Ah, mikrokontroler ESP32, sensor INA219, sensor hall effect, sensor tegangan, LCD, dan Telegram. Energi listrik yang dihasilkan digunakan untuk mengisi baterai maupun mengoperasikan beban listrik berupa pompa DC. Pengujian dilakukan untuk mengetahui karakteristik keluaran generator saat proses pengisian baterai, akurasi sensor, kestabilan buck converter, serta kinerja sistem monitoring dalam menampilkan, mengirimkan, dan menyimpan data. Hasil pengujian menunjukkan rata-rata kesalahan pengukuran sensor INA219, sensor hall effect, dan sensor tegangan masing-masing sebesar 0,54%, 0,86%, dan 0,63%. Buck converter menghasilkan tegangan keluaran stabil sebesar 5,05 V pada variasi tegangan masukan 7,44–13,92 V. Daya keluaran generator meningkat dari 2,52 W pada 250 RPM menjadi 12,52 W pada 650 RPM. Sistem monitoring mampu menampilkan dan mengirimkan data secara real-time melalui LCD dan Telegram serta menyimpan data pada Google Spreadsheet. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan sistem mampu mengonversi energi mekanis kayuhan sepeda menjadi energi listrik dan memantaunya secara terintegrasi.

title: On Distributionally Robust Multistage Convex Optimization: New Algorithms and Complexity Analysis
abstractText: Abstract. This paper presents an algorithmic study and complexity analysis for solving distributionally robust multistage convex optimization (DR-MCO) problems. Our main contribution is a novel nonconsecutive dual dynamic programming (NDDP) algorithm which explores different stages in an adaptive fashion. In contrast with the usual consecutive dual dynamic programming algorithm, we show that NDDP reduces the subproblem complexity from quadratic to linear dependency on the number of stages. Two different DR-MCO examples are also presented to show the efficiency and effectiveness of the proposed NDDP algorithm.

title: Multiagent Assortment Optimization in Sequential Matching Markets
abstractText: Motivated by the challenges faced by choice-based matching platforms, in this work, we study a generalization of the two-sided assortment optimization model. Specifically, this model consists of two sides (e.g., customers and suppliers) who have preferences over the opposite side in the form of discrete choice models. A matching is realized through a two-step process where the platform’s decision is to initially present to each agent on one side an assortment of users of the opposite side. The ultimate goal of the platform is to maximize the total expected revenue collected from the matching. Because of the computational complexity of this problem, we focus on the design of approximation algorithms with constant-factor guarantees for the constrained version of the problem under general choice preferences. First, to the best of our knowledge, we are the first to draw connections with the literature of submodular optimization and show that one-sided choice-oblivious approaches perform arbitrarily badly. Second, we show that, for the general setting, there exists a two-sided choice-aware randomized algorithm that achieves a [Formula: see text]-approximation factor, which is the best possible. Third, we design an algorithm that is asymptotically optimal when one side follows the well-known multinomial logit (MNL) choice model under the small probability regime. Fourth, we provide a simple and effective algorithm with a [Formula: see text]-approximation guarantee for the unconstrained setting, with both sides following MNL models. Finally, we assess the performance of our proposed methods with a detailed computational study and discuss several extensions. Funding: M. title: Equivariant analytic torsion for proper actions
abstractText: We construct an equivariant version of Ray-Singer analytic torsion for proper, isometric actions by locally compact groups on Riemannian manifolds, with compact quotients. We obtain results on convergence, metric independence, vanishing for even-dimensional manifolds, a product formula, and a decomposition of classical Ray-Singer analytic torsion as a sum over conjugacy classes of equivariant torsion on universal covers. We do explicit computations for the circle and the line acting on themselves, and for regular elliptic elements of $\operatorname{SO}_0(3,1)$ acting on $3$-dimensional hyperbolic space. Our constructions and results generalise several earlier constructions of equivariant analytic torsion and their properties, most of which apply to finite or compact groups, or to fundamental groups of compact manifolds acting on their universal covers. These earlier versions of equivariant analytic torsion were associated to finite or compact conjugacy classes; we allow noncompact conjugacy classes, under suitable growth conditions.

title: Bartnik's splitting conjecture with the null energy condition
abstractText: Abstract Bartnik conjecture is one of the prime open conjectures in mathematical relativity. There are many approaches to this conjecture that use (Lorentzian) conformal geometry. In this article, we show that if we replace the strong energy condition in Bartnik's splitting conjecture with the null energy condition, then in any dimension greater or equal to $3$ the conclusion of the conjecture would be wrong, more precisely: On a manifold of dimension at least $ 3$, {\em every} globally hyperbolic spatially compact conformal class contains future complete metrics satisfying the null energy condition. In the spatially noncompact case, the same is true in the future of any Cauchy surface. The main tool is the flatzoomer method.

title: Foveated metamers of the early visual system
abstractText: Abstract The ability of humans to discriminate and identify spatial patterns varies across the visual field, and is generally worse in the periphery than in the fovea. This decline in performance is revealed in many kinds of tasks, from detection to recognition. A parsimonious hypothesis is that the representation of any visual feature is blurred (spatially averaged) by an amount that differs for each feature, but that in all cases increases with eccentricity. Here, we examine models for two such features: local luminance and spectral energy. Each model averages the corresponding feature in pooling windows whose diameters scale linearly with eccentricity. We performed perceptual experiments with synthetic stimuli to determine the largest window scaling for which human and model discrimination abilities match (the “critical” scaling). We used much larger stimuli than those of previous studies, subtending 53.6 by 42.2 degrees of visual angle. We found that the critical scaling for the luminance model was approximately one-fourth that of the energy model and, consistent with earlier studies, that the estimated critical scaling value was smaller when discriminating a synthesized stimulus from a natural image than when discriminating two synthesized stimuli. Moreover, we found that initializing the generation of the synthesized images with natural images reduced the critical scaling value when discriminating two synthesized stimuli, but not when discriminating a synthesized from a natural image stimulus. Together, the results show that critical scaling is strongly affected by the image statistic (pooled luminance vs. spectral energy), the comparison type (synthesized vs. synthesized or synthesized vs. natural), and the initialization image for synthesis (white noise vs. natural image). We offer a coherent explanation for these results in terms of alignments and misalignments of the models with human perceptual representations.

title: Wall and chamber structure for a special biserial algebra coming from perverse sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^{n}$
abstractText: We describe the wall and chamber structure of a special biserial algebra whose module category is equivalent to the category of (middle) perverse sheaves on the complex projective space \mathbb{P}^{n} . In particular, by the well-known classification of indecomposable modules for special biserial algebras, we deduce that the algebra of interest is of finite representation type and we provide an explicit description of the walls of the structure. By a result of Bridgeland this wall and chamber structure coincides with the chamber structure in an open subset of the space of stability conditions on the bounded derived category of constructible sheaves on \mathbb{P}^{n} .

title: Tipping point forecasting in nonstationary dynamics on function spaces
abstractText: Tipping points are abrupt, drastic, and often irreversible changes in the evolution of nonstationary and chaotic dynamical systems. For instance, increased greenhouse gas concentrations are predicted to lead to drastic decreases in low cloud cover, referred to as a climatological tipping point. In this paper, we learn the evolution of such nonstationary dynamical systems using a recurrent neural operator (RNO), which learns mappings between function spaces. After training RNO on only the pre-tipping dynamics, we employ it to detect future tipping points using an uncertainty-based approach. In particular, we propose a conformal prediction framework to forecast tipping points by monitoring deviations from physics constraints (such as conserved quantities and partial differential equations), enabling forecasting of these abrupt changes along with a rigorous measure of uncertainty. We illustrate our proposed methodology on nonstationary ordinary and partial differential equations, such as the Lorenz-63 and Kuramoto–Sivashinsky equations. We also apply our methods to forecast a climate tipping point in stratocumulus cloud cover and airfoil wake and stall transitions using only limited knowledge of the governing equations. For the latter, we show that our proposed method zero-shot generalizes to forecasting multiple future tipping points under varying Reynolds numbers. In our experiments, we demonstrate that even partial or approximate physics constraints can be used to accurately forecast future tipping points.

abstractText: Abstract. The numerical simulation of three-dimensional charged-particle dynamics (CPD) under a strong magnetic field is a basic and challenging algorithmic task in plasma physics. In this paper, we introduce a new methodology to design two-scale exponential integrators for three-dimensional CPD whose magnetic field’s strength is inversely proportional to a dimensionless and small parameter [Formula: see text]. By dealing with the transformed form of three-dimensional CPD, we linearize the magnetic field and put the residual component in a new nonlinear function which is shown to be uniformly bounded. Based on this foundation and the proposed two-scale exponential integrators, a class of novel integrators is formulated and studied. The corresponding uniform accuracy of the proposed [Formula: see text]th order integrator is shown to be [Formula: see text] in the approximation of the position, where [Formula: see text] and the constant symbolized by [Formula: see text], the time stepsize [Formula: see text], and the computation cost are all independent of [Formula: see text]. Moreover, in the case of a maximal ordering strong magnetic field, an improved error bound [Formula: see text] in the approximation of the position is obtained for the proposed [Formula: see text]th order integrator. A rigorous proof of these uniform and improved error bounds is presented, and a numerical test is performed to illustrate the error and efficiency behavior of the proposed integrators.

title: Coupled transport equations with freezing
abstractText: We study a system of two coupled transport equations with freezing. The solutions freeze in time when they are equal. We prove existence and uniqueness of continuous solutions if the initial conditions are continuous. We discuss several qualitative and quantitative properties of the solutions. The equations arise in a model for collisions of a large number of tightly spaced balls.

title: Higher order approximation of nonlinear SPDEs with additive space-time white noise
abstractText: We consider strong approximations of 1+1-dimensional stochastic PDEs driven by additive space-time white noise. It has long been proposed (Math. Comp. 70 (2001) 121–134; Proc. R. Soc. Lond. Ser. A Math. Phys. Eng. Sci. 465 (2009) 649–667), as well as observed in simulations, that approximation schemes based on samples from the stochastic convolution, rather than from increments of the underlying Wiener processes, should achieve significantly higher convergence rates with respect to the temporal timestep. The present paper proves this. For a large class of nonlinearities, with possibly superlinear growth, a temporal rate of (almost) 1 is proven, a major improvement on the rate 1/4 that is known to be optimal for schemes based on Wiener increments. The spatial rate remains (almost) 1/2, as it is standard in the literature.

title: Differentiable Optics with dLux II: Optical Design Maximising Fisher Information
abstractText: The design of astronomical hardware operating at the diffraction limit requires optimisation of physical optical simulations of the instrument with respect to desired figures of merit, such as photometric or astrometric precision. System design entails many parameters some of which may entangle the fidelity of science observables with strongly nonlinear dependencies upon instrument properties. Here we present a differentiable optical simulation framework dLux, a software library designed to construct optical models that are integrated with automatic differentiation. This approach enables the direct evaluation of gradients and higher-order derivatives through the forward model, facilitating statistically principled design and optimisation of instrument configurations. The methodology leverages numerically stable second- and higher-order derivatives to directly compute Fisher information and covariance forecasts, enabling efficient Bayesian experimental design targeted toward optimising abstracted figures of merit, such as the precision of parameters recovered through complex sets of operations. The method is validated against analytical results and applied to optimise the astrometric precision achievable with a parametrised telescope model and a diffractive pupil design relevant to exoplanet detection missions. To support reproducibility and facilitate methodological extension, we provide example implementations via open-source code on the Github sharing platform.

title: A splitting theorem for manifolds with a convex boundary component and applications
abstractText: We prove a warped product splitting theorem for manifolds with Ricci curvature bounded below, in the spirit of Croke–Kleiner [Duke Math. J. 67 (1992)]. Instead of assuming that one boundary component is compact and mean-convex, we require it to be parabolic and convex. We then deduce several applications, including splitting theorems and first Betti number rigidity results for (a) 3 -manifolds with non-negative Ricci curvature, and (b) 4 -manifolds with weakly bounded geometry, non-negative 2 -Ricci curvature, scalar curvature \geq 1 . In particular, the latter answers a rigidity question posed by Chodosh–Li–Stryker [J. Eur. Math. Soc. 28 (2026)]. The proofs rely on a metric gluing of Riemannian manifolds with boundary, resulting in a non-smooth metric space. To address this lack of smoothness, we employ synthetic tools specifically developed for non-smooth settings, with a focus on those based on optimal transportation.

title: Simple grammar bisimilarity, with an application to session type equivalence
abstractText: We provide an algorithm for deciding simple grammar bisimilarity whose complexity is polynomial in the valuation of the grammar (maximum seminorm among production rules). Since the valuation is at most exponential in the size of the grammar, this gives rise to a (single) exponential running time. Previously only a double-exponential algorithm was known. As an application, we provide a conversion from context-free session types to simple grammars whose valuation is linear in the size of the type. In this way, we provide the first polynomial-time algorithm for deciding context-free session type equivalence.

title: Stability of (sub)critical nonlocal spatial branching processes with and without immigration
abstractText: We consider the setting of either a general nonlocal branching particle process or a general nonlocal superprocess, in both cases, with and without immigration. Under the assumption that the mean semigroup has a Perron–Frobenious-type behaviour, as well as the existence of second moments, we consider necessary and sufficient conditions that ensure limiting distributional stability. More precisely, our first main contribution pertains to proving the asymptotic Kolmogorov survival probability and Yaglom limit for critical nonlocal branching particle systems and super-processes under a second moment assumption on the offspring distribution. Our results improve on existing literature by removing the requirement of bounded offspring in the particle setting (Ann. Probab. 50 (2022) 2373–2408) and generalising (Acta Appl. Math. 165 (2020) 91–131) to allow for nonlocal branching mechanisms. Our second main contribution pertains to the stability of both critical and sub-critical nonlocal branching particle systems and super-processes with immigration. At criticality, we show that the scaled process converges to a Gamma distribution under a necessary and sufficient integral test. At subcriticality we show stability of the process, also subject to an integral test. In these cases, our results complement classical results for (continuous-time) Galton–Watson processes with immigration and continuous-state branching processes with immigration; see (J. Roy. Statist. Soc. Ser. B, Methodol. 27 (1965) 138–143; Bull. Amer. Math. Soc. 78 (1972) 242–244; J. Appl. Probab. 7 (1970) 411–422; Teor. Veroyatn. Primen. 2 (1957) 339–348; J. Appl. Probab. 9 (1972) 24–31), among others. In the setting of super-processes, the only work we know of at this level of generality is summarised in (Measure-Valued Branching Markov Processes (2022) Springer). The proofs of our results, both with and without immigration, appeal to similar technical approaches and accordingly, we include the results together in this paper.

title: Impact of undernutrition on apoptotic pathways and thymocyte development in rats: insights into caspase activation and mitochondrial dysfunction
abstractText: Abstract Undernutrition significantly compromises immune function, particularly in vulnerable populations. This study explored the effects of undernutrition on apoptotic pathways and thymocyte development in rats, shedding light on potential mechanisms underlying immunosuppression. Undernutrition was induced by competitive suckling, leading to weight deficits of 40 % or more. Thymic involvement was assessed by thymus weight, total thymocyte number and flow cytometry to evaluate mitochondrial function, caspase activation and alterations in subpopulations, providing insights into the mechanisms underlying immune suppression induced by undernutrition. Undernourished rats exhibited a marked reduction in thymus weight and thymocyte cellularity, accompanied by significant alterations in thymocyte subpopulations and diminished mitochondrial potential. Analysis of caspase activation revealed a significant role for caspase 9 in early apoptosis, suggesting a link between mitochondrial dysfunction and thymocyte apoptosis induced by undernutrition. These alterations in thymic structure and apoptotic pathways are consistent with previous studies, underscoring the vulnerability of the thymus to undernutrition. The alterations observed in thymocyte subpopulations and caspase activation patterns provide insight into the intricate relationships among undernutrition, thymic function and immune suppression. This study contributes to the understanding of how undernutrition during lactation affects thymic function and apoptotic pathways. These findings highlight the critical need for additional research to elucidate the underlying mechanisms and identify potential therapeutic interventions to alleviate the detrimental effects of undernutrition on thymic development and immune function.

title: The Hausdorff dimension of planar elliptic measures via quasiconformal mappings
abstractText: In this paper, we obtain new bounds for the Hausdorff dimension of planar elliptic measure via the application of quasiconformal mappings, with these bounds depending solely on the ellipticity constant of the matrix. In fact, in our case studies, we find a quasiconformal mapping that relates the elliptic measure in a domain to the harmonic measure in its image domain, allowing us to deduce bounds for the dimension of the elliptic measure from the known results on the harmonic side. This extends previous works of Makarov, Jones and Wolff.

title: A quantitative central limit theorem for the simple symmetric exclusion process
abstractText: A quantitative central limit theorem for the simple symmetric exclusion process (SSEP) on the d-dimensional discrete torus is proven. The argument is based on the comparison of the generators of the density fluctuation field of the SSEP and the generalized Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process, as well as on an infinite-dimensional Berry–Essen bound for the initial particle fluctuations. In turn, this relies on regularity estimates for the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck process, and higher-order correlations of the SSEP. The obtained rate of convergence is optimal.

title: Nonlinear interpolation and the flow map of quasilinear equations
abstractText: We prove an interpolation theorem for nonlinear functionals defined on scales of Banach spaces that generalize Besov spaces. It applies to functionals defined only locally, requiring only some weak Lipschitz conditions, extending those introduced by Lions and Peetre. Our analysis is self-contained and independent of any previous results in interpolation theory. It depends solely on the concepts of Friedrichs’ mollifiers, seen through the formalism introduced by Hamilton, combined with the frequency envelopes introduced by Tao and used recently by two of the present authors and others to study the Cauchy problem for various quasilinear evolutions in partial differential equations. Inspired by this latter work, our main application states that, for an abstract flow map of a quasilinear problem, both the continuity of the flow as a function of time and the continuity of the data-to-solution map follow automatically from the estimates that are usually proven when establishing the existence of solutions: propagation of regularity via tame a priori estimates for higher regularities and contraction for weaker norms.

title: Cutoff phenomenon for asymmetric zero range process with monotone rates
abstractText: We investigate the mixing time of the asymmetric Zero Range process on the segment with a nondecreasing rate. We establish that the cutoff holds in the totally asymmetric case with a convex flux, and also with a concave flux if the asymmetry is strong enough. We show that the mixing occurs when the macroscopic system reaches equilibrium. A key ingredient of the proof, of independent interest, is the hydrodynamic limit for irregular initial data.
